summary: Use selected edges to expose construction or relationships, deciding whether the view shows mesh topology, component outlines or an abstract graph.
objective: Dense rear edges do not overwhelm the selected structure and the legend identifies what a line represents.
intent_signals: Reveal selected edges and explain their meaning
example_prompts: Show a wireframe mechanical assembly with selected component edges and an optional solid reference view.

principles: Use selected edges to expose construction or relationships, deciding whether the view shows mesh topology, component outlines or an abstract graph.
implementation: Choose meaningful edges and suppress irrelevant tessellation where the task permits; preserve the distinction between a true mesh edge and an annotation.
Set line contrast against a quiet fill or background; optionally combine translucent surfaces and highlighted selected edges.
Offer orbit and a focus/isolation view; animate meaningful edits or component motion while keeping edge identities comprehensible.

Build edges with new THREE.EdgesGeometry(geometry, 30) so only feature edges survive tessellation, then draw the occluded pass as the same geometry with depthTest false and opacity 0.3; use Line2/LineMaterial when a width above 1 px is needed.

Keep line #6fd0ff on background #0b1b2b for roughly 6:1 contrast, reserve #ffffff for the selected edge and #ffb347 for annotation and dimension lines; run with fog off, dof off and antialiasing on, because any blur destroys the only signal in the image.
observable_checks: Dense rear edges do not overwhelm the selected structure and the legend identifies what a line represents.

defaults.rationale: A wireframe image is 80% background, so the composition is line density and the palette exists only to keep three line jobs apart: structure in cyan, selection in white, annotation in amber. Fog, depth of field and bloom are all set to none because a 1 px line carries no gradient to blur - depth is expressed instead by dropping occluded edges to 0.3 opacity - and Neutral tone mapping at exposure 1.0 keeps the flat line colours exactly as authored.

palette.role: annotation and dimension lines, never mesh edges

values.value_structure: 80/12/8 dark/mid/light; the frame is mostly empty background so line density itself is the composition
values.saturation_rule: one cyan line family plus one amber annotation family; occluded lines drop to 30% opacity rather than changing hue

key.note: LineSegments with LineBasicMaterial are unlit; edge colour is authored, not shaded

lights.ratio: unlit lines; the optional translucent shell is lit only by the 0.35 hemisphere so it can never out-value a line

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

camera.projection: orthographic preferred for reading topology; perspective at fov 30 only when depth ordering must be disambiguated

materials.notes: LineSegments with LineBasicMaterial at #6fd0ff, linewidth 1 (Line2/LineMaterial above 1 px); occluded edges as a second pass at opacity 0.3 with depthTest false; optional shell as MeshBasicMaterial at opacity 0.08

values.signature_technique: two-pass edges - visible edges at full opacity plus the same EdgesGeometry redrawn with depthTest false at 0.3 opacity - so hidden structure is present without competing
never: fog or depth-of-field blur on lines
annotation and mesh edges sharing one colour
full tessellation edges where EdgesGeometry at 30 degrees is enough

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for Neutral tone mapping at exposure 1.0; re-tune every intensity, fog density and bloom threshold if you change the tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with technical illustration or holographic presentation; a wireframe skin does not itself validate topology or hidden structure.
